reason: The lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure and phase compositions are directly supported by E2 and E3. However, the cited evidence provides no data on differential oxidation kinetics, oxide spallation under wear, or galvanic coupling between phases in this alloy. E5 discusses pitting of Al-Ni-rich phases in a corrosive solution but does not involve mechanical wear or elevated temperature synergy. E4 concerns a different alloy and does not address the proposed mechanism. The core mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure with Al-Ni-rich and Co-Cr-Fe-rich regions
Differential oxidation kinetics occur between the anodic (Al-Ni-rich) and cathodic (Co-Cr-Fe-rich) phases
Mechanical wear causes spallation of the oxide film, exposing fresh anodic metal
Exposed anodic sites form localized galvanic cells with cathodic regions, accelerating corrosion
This synergy leads to degradation significantly higher than wear or corrosion alone
